newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Cisco gets busy ahead of earnings.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Cisco gets busy ahead of earnings.

text.p: Options on shares of Cisco Systems Inc turned active Tuesday ahead of the company's fourth quarter earnings, which are scheduled for release after the U.S. stock market closes.
"There really hasn't been much interest in it coming up to today," Patrick Hamilton at LETCO said of Cisco options trading. "Today's been the first day where we've had some business."
He said the lack of pre-earnings options activity in Cisco kept volatilities in the mid-50's. Volatility in Cisco often rises through 70 ahead of earnings.
By about 1125 CST/1625 GMT, Cisco shares were up 1-3/8 at 83 on heavy turnover of about 4.9 million shares.
The company is expected to report a 34 percent jump in fiscal fourth quarter earnings.

According to Zacks Investment Research, Wall Street analysts are expecting the networking company to post $0.55 per share earnings, but traders said some unpublished forecasts call for profits of up to $0.60 a share.
Hamilton said that in terms of the options, investors appeared to be looking for good news.
"There's pretty much been buyers of calls," he said. "The paper is telling me right now it looks like they're expecting it to go up."
The busiest Cisco options included the August 80 calls, which traded 2,850 contracts, the August 85 calls, which traded 1,800 and the September 85 calls, which traded 1,735.
Hamilton said the September 85 call volume was from an investor selling them as part of a buy-write strategy.
In other activity, Micron Technology Inc had some active options as the stock continued to move higher.
Micron shares were ahead two at 53-9/16 --their highest level since mid-December 1995 -- on consolidated turnover of 3.8 million shares.
"I think the stock has fundamentally lagged behind other techs and people are starting to realize that," said Rob Kovell, the lead market maker in Micron options at the Pacific Exchange.
He said, however, that the options flow was not indicating whether investors were betting on a further rise in the stock or a pullback.
"The order flow isn't saying anything particular one way or the other," he said, adding that speculators were driving the options volumes.
Most activity was in the Micron August 55 calls, which traded a total of about 4,315 contracts.
Kovell said some of that volume was crossed, most likely by an investor doing a buy-write as opposed to a speculator.
He added that with Micron earnings due in September, some investors were buying the September-August spreads, which helped pump September volatility up higher than the other months.
